newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 9.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - On Wednesday the cabinet decided that Boeing and McDonnell Douglas together with Czech Airlines will be the strategic partner of the largest domestic aircraft manufacturer Aero Vodochody. The winner should increase the company's capital from 950 million to up to 2.5 billion crowns, for which it will receive 34 percent of shares.
- The City Court in Prague decided on Wednesday that the five-day strike at Czech Railways in February was against the law, which could cost the union about 30 million crowns in damages.
- Vitkovice obtained a contract for the supply and assembly of transport and handling machinery for the new rolling track of SSAB Oxelosund, the largest Swedish manufacturer of heavy sheet metal.
- Fatra Napajedla became the sole owner of Technoplast Chropyne and took up all places in its statutary organs.
- According to Miroslav Havel from the Finance Ministry, the government budget for 1998 should have revenue and expenses of 560.9 billion crowns.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Investicni a Postovni Banka does not plan on changing its two senior directors who are currently in jail. One of the points of its last general meeting called for changes in personnel, which, according to spokesman Jan Rezek, mean increasing personnel.

- Imports of oil and oil products from EU countries increased during the first quarter of this year by 82 percent year-on-year to 1.1513 billion crowns. Oil imports from CEFTA countries increased by 57 percent to 1.493 billion crowns.
PRAVO - Tatra Koprivnice expects to be profitable this year, and its turnover should be between eight and nine billion crowns, according to its financial director Jan Ludva.
- The holding company VSZ confirmed that it is meeting with Nomura bank about building an automobile factory in Slovakia.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The replacement for Regional Development Minister Jaromir Schneider, who resigned on April 29 on the request of his party the Christian Democrats, will be his deputy Tomas Kvapil.

- On Wednesday, the cabinet approved a proposal for a new law on social security insurance and contributions to the state employment policy. The new law will increase the daily penalty for businesses which don't pay from 0.025 percent of the amount owed to 0.035 percent daily.
- According to an agreement between public radio station Cesky Rozhlas and private broadcasters, payments for using a radio will increase by two crowns to 37 crowns monthly.
- Although doctors and nurses did not obtain their demands, they brought an end to the strike in Motol Hospital. They will remain ready to strike and will discuss other possible protests today.
- The Liechtenstein company Blax Corporation, which owns 50.3 percent of Poldi Steel, began preparations to renew operations at Poldi, with the help of Trinecke Zelezarny.
